source.title: The Representational Limit of Scalar Interactions: An Interventional Decomposition
source.authors: Potito Aghilar; Sabino Roccotelli; Stanislao Fidanza; V. W. Anelli; S. Stramaglia; T. D. Noia

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates GPT-2 small IOI head contributions using mean-ablation coalition decomposition, a different method from the original circuit-discovery tests. It reports head- and role-pair results bearing on the circuit's proposed functional roles.
record.gate_note: The paper analyzes a 10-head subset and a 26-head candidate set, but does not test the original circuit's faithfulness, completeness, or minimality criteria, or whether removing everything outside it changes IOI performance. Its single-head patching correlation is described as an algebraic identity, not independent validation. Claims cited from the original IOI work are not treated as results of this study.
record.test_reason: The paper uses the IOI head set from the original as a ready-made testbed to show that its own U/R/S decomposition (Stochastic Hi-Fi) separates redundant from synergistic heads. Head roles are taken from the original and never tested. The paper itself frames E3 as asking whether 'the decomposition recovers a transformer circuit'. No result bears on faithfulness, completeness, minimality, backup takeover, transfer to other models, recovery by other methods, or prompt variants. The per-head and role-pair values describe the method's output on the given heads, not whether the circuit claim holds. Its validity check (r39) is an algebraic identity.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors claim more than the record says. They state the decomposition 'recovers the known circuit structure' and stays 'structurally faithful' at 26 heads. They say pre-registered predictions hold: within-role pairs are redundancy-dominated and cross-role compositional pairs synergy-dominated. They also say heads 'invisible to activation patching' carry pair-level synergy. They present this as validating their method against the known circuit, not as testing the circuit. They do not claim faithfulness, completeness or minimality.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Stochastic Hi-Fi interventional mean-ablation coalition losses and LOCO U/R/S extrema, rather than the original circuit-discovery procedure. It exhaustively evaluates the coalition lattice for the 10-head analysis and reports a 26-head extension.

fits_no_version.finding: Under mean ablation within the candidate head set, head pairs show measurable synergy and redundancy. Induction+S-Inhibition is synergy-dominated (S̄ 0.475, R̄ 0.045); Duplicate-Token+Induction is redundancy-dominated (R̄ 0.244). Several name-mover heads have negative singleton π but large synergy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contributions of IOI circuit heads are strongly non-additive: some heads with near-zero or negative single-head patching effect carry large pairwise synergy.

record.problems: The 26-head per-head results in Table 12 do not state uncertainty values. The reported singleton patching-score correlation is an algebraic identity. The analysis does not test whether the candidate circuit is complete or minimal.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports a 10-head analysis, its role-pair summaries, subset perturbation checks, and variance-reduction diagnostics. These were not included because the 26-head per-head and role-pair results were retained for the tested circuit-role version; other results concern estimator performance rather than whether the original IOI circuit claim holds.

untested.parts: Faithfulness, completeness and minimality of the 26-head circuit; the head classes are assumed from the original, not derived.
Takeover by backup heads after name-mover ablation; only a reinterpretation of negative U for 9.6.
Recovery of the circuit by other discovery methods; only the 26 given heads are decomposed.
Dependence of faithfulness/completeness on ablation, metric or prompt distribution; only mean ablation with an ABC-corrupted mean is used.
ABBA and BABA are pooled; no per-template or per-name-order results.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is an XAI-method paper; IOI is one of three testbeds. There are internal inconsistencies. The body claims within-role blocks are redundancy-dominated, yet within S-Inhibition S̄=0.200 vs R̄=0.039 at n=10, and S̄≈R̄ at n=26. Table 5 and Table 11 report different pair counts for the same role pairs. Appendix H.2 says the original circuit has 'roughly 15' heads, while H.3 uses 26. The named negative name movers (10.7, 11.10) show the largest positive π, and name movers 9.9 and 10.0 show negative π. This would be odd under the original roles, but the paper does not examine it, and the context (all other candidate heads ablated) differs from the original's tests. Values for the same heads differ between the 10-head and 26-head runs because the context set changes. The Appendix H.5.1 E2 text has contradictory p-values (0.140 vs 0.998). Not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: Tests IOI head and role-pair contributions for the 26-head candidate set using mean-ablation coalition decomposition. Does not test faithfulness, completeness, minimality, or the effect of removing everything outside the circuit.

Does not test whether other heads take over when main name-mover heads are ablated. It interprets negative uniqueness for head 9.6 as consistent with known backup behavior, but does not test takeover.
No other model, size, checkpoint, or task is tested for reuse of these circuit components.
Does not compare circuit recovery across alternative circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics. The singleton patching-score identity is not such a comparison.
Does not compare ablations, metrics, or prompt distributions to test their effects on faithfulness or completeness, or whether the circuit explains only part of IOI behavior.
Uses ABBA/BABA prompts together but does not report separate results by name order, template, or number of names, or test whether other formats use the same components.

rows.operation_detail: Compare singleton LOCO π rankings with mean-ablation activation-patching scores
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between singleton LOCO π and activation-patching scores
rows.value: 1.000 (reported as 0.9999999999999998 ± 1.11 × 10−16, exact up to floating-point precision)
rows.note: The paper calls this an algebraic identity by construction, not independent evidence that the full circuit is recovered.
rows.check: An algebraic identity between the method's π and single-head patching, true by construction. It is a check on the study's own method, not a result on the claim, and should not be a row.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT 2-SMALL, 26-head candidate set, mean-ablation coalition decomposition
reader_labels.reason: Per-head and role-pair results show differentiated IOI contributions, including reported synergy- and redundancy-dominated combinations, consistent with functional head roles (r1–r38). The singleton patching-score ranking identity is also reported (r39), but is not independent circuit validation.
